overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Husserl's account of the lived body. You'll be asked about the Leib/Körper distinction, Empfindnisse, the double sensation, the zero point of orientation, and kinaesthesis.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: How does Husserl understand the relation between the Leib and the Körper?

options.html: They're two different bodies, one inner and one outer
options.text: They're two different bodies, one inner and one outer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. There's one body. The Leib and the Körper are that one body given in two ways: as lived from within, and as a physical thing.

options.html: They're one body given in two ways: as lived and as a thing
options.text: They're one body given in two ways: as lived and as a thing
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The body is the only thing given both as a physical thing (Körper) and as lived from within (Leib).

options.html: The Leib is the mind, and the Körper is the physical body
options.text: The Leib is the mind, and the Körper is the physical body
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The Leib isn't the mind. It's the body itself, given as lived from within.

options.html: The Leib is the body seen in a mirror, the Körper as felt
options.text: The Leib is the body seen in a mirror, the Körper as felt
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. It's the reverse. The body seen in a mirror is the Körper, and the body felt from within is the Leib.

forms.stemHtml: When your right hand touches your left, what makes the left hand a lived body and not just a physical thing?

options.html: It has smoothness and warmth that the right hand perceives
options.text: It has smoothness and warmth that the right hand perceives
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Smoothness and warmth are properties any physical thing can have. What makes the left hand lived is that sensings, the feeling of being touched, are localized in it.

options.html: Sensings of being touched are felt in the left hand itself
options.text: Sensings of being touched are felt in the left hand itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sensings (Empfindnisse) are sensations localized in the lived body and felt there. A table can be touched, but it has no sensings.

options.html: It can be seen clearly when you look at it
options.text: It can be seen clearly when you look at it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Seeing the hand presents it as a physical thing. What makes it lived is that sensings, the feeling of being touched, are localized in it.

options.html: It's attached to the same arm that holds the right hand
options.text: It's attached to the same arm that holds the right hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Physical attachment doesn't make a body part lived. What does is that sensings, the feeling of being touched, are localized in it.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are features of the lived body, on Husserl's account? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It is the zero point of orientation, always "here"
options.text: It is the zero point of orientation, always "here"
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The lived body is the absolute "here" from which everything else is "there."

options.html: It is moved immediately and spontaneously by the will
options.text: It is moved immediately and spontaneously by the will
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The lived body is the organ of the will, the one thing moved directly by willing.

options.html: It is perceived mainly by seeing it from outside
options.text: It is perceived mainly by seeing it from outside
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Seeing the body from outside presents it as a physical thing. The lived body is first given through touch.

options.html: It is the bearer of localized sensings
options.text: It is the bearer of localized sensings
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Sensings are felt in the lived body itself.

forms.stemHtml: What is Husserl's term for the felt sense of one's own movement, including movements of the eyes, head, and limbs? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Kinaesthesis is the felt sense of one's own movement. Perception is organized by the correlation between it and changes in appearance.
Correct! Kinaesthesis (also spelled kinesthesis) is the felt sense of one's own movement.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The felt sense of one's own movement is kinaesthesis.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Husserl hold that touch, not vision, first gives the body as lived?

options.html: Vision is less reliable than touch about physical properties
options.text: Vision is less reliable than touch about physical properties
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The point isn't reliability. Touch localizes sensings in the body itself, while vision presents the body only as a thing, because the eye doesn't see itself.

options.html: Touch localizes sensings in the body; the eye doesn't see itself
options.text: Touch localizes sensings in the body; the eye doesn't see itself
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! When one hand touches the other, sensings are felt in it. Vision presents even one's own body only as a thing, because visual sensations aren't localized in the eye.

options.html: Touch requires movement, while vision works without movement
options.text: Touch requires movement, while vision works without movement
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Both involve movement and kinaesthesis. The difference is that touch localizes sensings in the body, while the eye doesn't see itself.

options.html: Vision can present only distant objects, not nearby ones
options.text: Vision can present only distant objects, not nearby ones
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Vision presents near objects too, including one's own hand, but only as a thing. Touch localizes sensings in the body itself.

title: The Lived Body
